newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Somprasong watched on bond payment.
newsitem.headline: Thai Somprasong watched on bond payment.

text.p: Thai cash-strapped property developer Somprasong Land Plc will have until February 4 to come up with 79 million baht (US$3.1 million) to pay interest in its euroconvertible debenture to holders, sources closed to the deal said on Friday.
It will also have to pay the government 14 million baht in withholding tax, the sources said.

A Somprasong official declined to comment and did not say if the company has already transferred the money to its paying agent Bankers Trust in London. The interest was due on Tuesday, but the company has a 14-day grace period to meet the obligation.
If the company fails to come up with the money, it will be the first Thai firm to default on a Eurobond.
The company on Friday cancelled its shareholders meeting without explanation.
Somprasong in January 1994 issued the $80-million Eurobond, which will mature in 1999.
The company is among those in Thailand's depressed property sector, which is being battered by oversupply and cash flow problems.

Recently, four major financial institutions, including Bangkok Bank, Siam Commercial Bank, National Finance and Securities and Ekachart Finance and Securities, announced they would set up a 1.8- billion baht fund to buy prime land owned by Somprasong.
